CSCA Exam Format 2026–27: Questions, Timing and Scoring

CSCA exam format: 48 questions in 60 minutes for Math, Physics and Chemistry; 80 in 90 for Professional Chinese. See scoring and official sample questions.

CSCA.ai Editorial Team

How is the CSCA scored?

How should you prepare for the CSCA exam format?

Frequently asked questions

The CSCA exam format is simple: every question is single-choice. Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry each have 48 questions in 60 minutes, offered in Chinese or English. Professional Chinese has 80 questions in 90 minutes, in Chinese only. Each subject is scored from 0 to 100, and there is no single official pass mark.

Exam: China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA), the admission test for international applicants to undergraduate programs at Chinese universities

Subjects: Professional Chinese (Humanities or STEM track), Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry

Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry: 48 single-choice questions, 60 minutes each, in Chinese or English

Professional Chinese: 80 single-choice questions, 90 minutes, Chinese only

Scoring: 0–100 in each subject, reported separately

Maximum score: 100 per subject; there is no official combined total

Pass mark: none set nationally; each university sets its own requirement

Calculator: Check the candidate instructions for your sitting; prepare to work without one

Results: the current official exam introduction says scores are released within 10 working days after the exam; check your sitting notice.

If you are new to the test, start with our overview of what the CSCA exam is and who needs it. One quick note on the name: CSCA is also an accounting certificate from the IMA (Certified in Strategy and Competitive Analysis). This guide is only about the China Scholastic Competency Assessment, the test for students applying to bachelor's programs in China.

The organizer provides Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry sample-question downloads on its official CSCA preparation resources page. These show the question style, but they are samples rather than complete past papers. For worked explanations of independently written practice, read our CSCA exam questions guide.

What is the CSCA exam format?

The CSCA has four subjects, but you sit only the papers required for your application route and target programs. Mathematics is required for every applicant; Physics and Chemistry depend on your major and university. The official CSCA exam introduction lists Professional Chinese for Chinese Government Scholarship undergraduate applicants, while the Shanghai government CSCA guide says applicants to fully English-taught undergraduate programs are exempt. These published instructions differ. If you are applying to a fully English-taught scholarship program, confirm the exact requirement with your target university or scholarship office before booking. For other applicants, Professional Chinese is required for Chinese-taught programs. Choose the Humanities or STEM track your university specifies. For dates, fees and registration, see our CSCA exam 2026–27 guide.

Mathematics: 48 single-choice questions, 60 minutes, Chinese or English, scored 0–100. Required for all applicants.

Physics: 48 single-choice questions, 60 minutes, Chinese or English, scored 0–100. Required by many science, engineering and medical programs.

Chemistry: 48 single-choice questions, 60 minutes, Chinese or English, scored 0–100. Required by many science, medical and agriculture programs.

Professional Chinese (Humanities or STEM): 80 single-choice questions, 90 minutes, Chinese only, scored 0–100. Required for Chinese-taught programs. The official exam introduction also lists it for Chinese Government Scholarship applicants, but Shanghai government guidance exempts fully English-taught applicants. Confirm your route and track with your university or scholarship office.

Every question is single-choice: you pick the one correct option from the choices given. There are no essays, no written solutions and no partial credit for working shown on paper. This makes the CSCA a test of two things at once: whether you know the high school content, and whether you can apply it quickly and accurately under time pressure.

Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry are offered in Chinese or English. Choose a paper language your target universities accept, then use the language in which you can answer most accurately under time pressure. The official CSCA exam introduction says to follow each university’s application requirements when selecting a language. Professional Chinese is always taken in Chinese. Our guide to the CSCA Professional Chinese test explains the Humanities and STEM tracks.

How long is the CSCA exam?

Each science subject lasts 60 minutes and Professional Chinese lasts 90 minutes. That works out to about 75 seconds per question in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, and about 67 seconds per question in Professional Chinese. Your total CSCA exam time depends on how many subjects you take: Mathematics alone is one hour, while Professional Chinese, Mathematics and Physics add up to three and a half hours of testing.

The official CSCA calendar now lists two-day sittings from 14–15 November 2026 through 26–27 June 2027. The November registration window closed on 21 October 2026; later sittings have separate windows. Start times and paper arrangements should be checked in the current organiser notice and your admission ticket, in Beijing Time (UTC+8). Convert the confirmed time to your local zone before test day. Our CSCA exam dates guide tracks the published sessions and deadlines.

How is the CSCA scored?

Each subject is scored on a scale from 0 to 100, and each subject is reported separately. Your score comes from the single-choice questions you answer correctly. Because 48 questions do not divide evenly into 100 points, some weighting or conversion must be used, but the official notices we checked do not publish the exact formula. Be careful with websites that claim to turn your raw answers into an exact CSCA score.

The official information we reviewed does not mention negative marking for wrong answers. If the candidate rules on csca.cn confirm this when you register, the sensible strategy is to answer every question, even if you have to make an educated guess in the final minute. Remove the options you know are wrong first, then choose.

What is the CSCA max score?

The CSCA max score is 100 in each subject. There is no official combined total. Some students add their subject scores together, for example 300 for three subjects, but that is an informal number. A university can look at each subject on its own, so a strong Mathematics score may not make up for a weak Physics score if your program cares about both. Ask your target university how it reads results from several subjects.

Is there a CSCA minimum score or pass rate?

No single official pass mark exists for the CSCA. It is not a pass or fail exam. Instead, each university sets its own requirements, and these can differ by program and by scholarship. Some university notices describe CSCA scores as a minimum admission criterion, while others describe them as one reference in an overall academic review.

The same goes for the CSCA exam pass rate: no official pass rate has been published, and without a national pass mark the idea does not really apply. If a website quotes a pass rate or a fixed cut-off score without linking to a university or official source, treat it as a guess. The reliable way to find your minimum score is your target university's admission guide, its admissions office, or the scholarship notice you are applying under.

Does the CSCA allow a calculator?

Plan to work without a calculator. The official CSCA exam introduction does not grant calculator use, and the organiser’s user agreement refers candidates to the notices and rules for their sitting. Check the permitted-items instructions in your csca.cn account and on your admission ticket; do not bring a calculator unless those instructions explicitly allow it. For preparation, practise fractions, squares, roots and standard trigonometric values by hand.

Two original teaching examples show the pace to aim for; they are not official CSCA questions or past-paper items. If (3/4)x = 18, multiply by 4/3 to get x = 24, then check that three quarters of 24 is 18. In Physics, a 2 kg object accelerating at 3 m/s² has net force F = ma = 6 N. Write the unit as well as the number. Aim to solve short calculations like these within roughly 75 seconds. Scratch-paper and desk rules can differ between home-based and test-centre sittings, so read the candidate instructions before exam day. Build speed with free CSCA mathematics practice questions while your calculator is out of reach.

CSCA currently lists home-based online and onsite computer-based tests. Check the formats available for your country and sitting on csca.cn.

If you test at home, plan for a reliable computer that meets the current technical requirements, a camera for proctoring, stable internet and a quiet private room. Use our home-based CSCA exam checklist to work through the device and room setup, then confirm each requirement on csca.cn for your sitting. Run any official system check well before exam day. For check-in and test-day rules, read our CSCA exam day tips.

What is on the CSCA score report?

CSCA results are released through your account on csca.cn, with a separate score for each subject. The official CSCA exam introduction, checked on 3 November 2026, says results are released within 10 working days after the exam. Check the notice for your sitting and your account for any update. Our CSCA results and score-report guide explains the next application steps and why there is no national pass mark.

Universities set their own score deadlines. For 2026 entry, some universities accepted a screenshot of your registration confirmation with the application and the actual scores later; Northwestern Polytechnical University, for example, asked for final scores by May 20, 2026. Our CSCA registration guide explains how to save that confirmation.

The CSCA FAQ published by the Chinese Embassy in Solomon Islands states that each score is valid for two years and that applicants may submit their best valid score, subject to the receiving university’s policy. Check the date on your report and the university’s current admissions instructions before using a score for a later intake. Our CSCA retake and score-validity guide explains how to compare sittings and deadlines. Reviewed 25 October 2026.

How should you prepare for the CSCA exam format?

Illustration of exam preparation subjects and timing. CSCA.ai artwork; this is not an official exam paper.

Knowing the format tells you how to train. These are the habits that matter most:

Confirm your subjects and paper language for each target program before you study anything else.

Learn the official syllabus topic by topic, starting with Mathematics, which everyone takes.

Train your pace to about 75 seconds per question in the science subjects.

Practice without a calculator from day one.

Take full 60-minute timed mocks, and 90-minute mocks if you sit Professional Chinese.

Review every wrong answer and write down why the wrong option looked right.

To see every topic you can be tested on, read the CSCA mathematics syllabus for 2026 and tick off what your school has already covered.

Then turn that list into a schedule with our 90-day CSCA study plan, which builds timed mock exams into the final month.

Frequently asked questions

CSCA FAQ

01

What is the CSCA max score?

Each subject is scored out of 100. There is no official combined total; every subject you take is reported on its own 0–100 scale.

02

What is the CSCA minimum score for Chinese universities?

There is no national minimum. Each university, and sometimes each program or scholarship, sets its own requirement, so check your target university's admission guide.

03

What is the CSCA exam pass rate?

No official pass rate has been published, and the CSCA has no national pass mark. Treat any pass rate you see online as unofficial.

04

Does the CSCA allow a calculator?

Plan to work without one. The public exam introduction does not grant calculator use; check the candidate instructions for your sitting on csca.cn and your admission ticket before taking any item into the exam.

05

How long is the CSCA exam?

Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry are 60 minutes each, and Professional Chinese is 90 minutes. Your total time depends on how many subjects you take.

06

How is the CSCA scored?

Each subject is scored from 0 to 100 based on your answers to single-choice questions. The exact conversion formula has not been published.

07

When do CSCA results come out?

The current official CSCA exam introduction says results are released within 10 working days after the exam. Check your sitting’s notice and log in to csca.cn to see each subject score.

08

Can I take the CSCA in English?

Yes for Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, which are offered in Chinese or English. Professional Chinese is in Chinese only.
